label: Pythagorean Theorem
overview: The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right triangle, the sum of the squares of the two legs equals the square of the hypotenuse. SAT questions use this to find missing sides, verify right angles, and work with Pythagorean triples. It also underpins the distance formula on the coordinate plane.

workedExamples.problem: A right triangle has legs 5 and 12. What is the length of the hypotenuse?

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding the legs without squaring: c = a + b
commonMistakes.fix: You must square each leg first, add the squares, then take the square root. The hypotenuse is never the simple sum of the legs.

commonMistakes.mistake: Labeling a leg as c instead of the hypotenuse
commonMistakes.fix: c is always the hypotenuse — the longest side, opposite the right angle. The two shorter sides are a and b (the legs).

quickTip: Recognize Pythagorean triples (3-4-5, 5-12-13) and their multiples to skip calculation entirely on many SAT questions.
